headline: world briefing | europe: russia: chechnya school siege toll up to 334
abstract: death toll from terrorist siege of middle school in beslan, chechnya, in 2004 rises to 334 when hostage, yelena avdonina, dies from internal bleeding (s)

headline: looking for a gambit to win at google’s game
abstract: article on efforts by microsoft to compete with google in internet business; microsoft's online properties have lost users in us over last year and billions of dollars it has spent to build its own search engine have yet to pay off; steve berkowitz, who heads microsoft's online services unit, comments on changes that have been made and those that are planned; photos; graphs (m)

headline: russia: school siege toll up to 334
abstract: the death toll from the terrorist siege of middle school no. 1 in beslan in 2004 rose to 334 when a hostage, yelena avdonina, 33, died from internal bleeding, news reports said. ms. avdonina was held along with her two children, who survived her, and died after being treated since the siege in moscow and rostov-on-don, in southern russia, the reports said. the toll includes the hostages, among them 186 children, and 12 rescuers, who died when the siege by chechen-led fighters ended in a convulsion of violence.

headline: china, shy giant, shows signs of shedding its false modesty
abstract: china's communist party has new agenda: it is encouraging people to discuss what it means to be major world power and has largely stopped denying that china intends to become one soon; its tradition of modesty has begun to fade, replaced by growing confidence that china's rise is not fleeting and that country needs to do more to define its objectives; beijing has begun asserting its interests far beyond its borders, with $1 trillion in foreign exchange reserves, surging military spending and diplomatic initiatives in asia, africa, and middle east; china's main television network has broadcast 12-part documentary describing reasons nine nations rose to become great powers; photos (m)

headline: iraqis near deal on distribution of oil revenues
abstract: iraqi officials are near agreement on national oil law that would give central government power to distribute oil revenues to provinces or regions, based on their populations; measure could help resolve divisive issue that has blocked efforts to reconcile country's feuding ethnic and sectarian factions; sunni arabs, who lead insurgency, have opposed idea of regional autonomy for fear that they would be deprived of fair share of country's oil wealth, which is concentrated in shiite south and kurdish north; iraq study group report stressed that oil law guaranteeing equitable distribution of revenues was crucial to process of national reconciliation, and to ending war; photo (m)

headline: northwest air to hire adviser, and talk of a merger starts
abstract: northwest airlines plans to hire evercore partners as financial adviser, signaling airline may be considering merger; analysts say most likely suitors are american airlines and delta air lines (m)

headline: democrats plan oil royalties inquiry
abstract: house democratic leaders, after defeat of measure that would have pressured oil companies to give up legal loop hole that is expected to allow them to avoid as much as $10 billion in royalties over next five years, vow to pursue broad overhaul of tax breaks and other subsidies to oil companies; says first step will be investigation of how government collects billions of dollars in royalties on oil and gas produced on federal property; incoming house resources committee chairman nick rahall says he plans sweeping probe of interior department's enforcement of royalty payments and possible repeal of law that allows energy companies drilling in deep coastal waters to avoid billions of dollars in payments; photos (m)

headline: correction: lights, camera, no parking
abstract: a picture caption last sunday with an article about a new union of film-crew parking assistants misidentified the production that used the street corner shown in the photograph. it was "p.s., i love you," a film described in the article's first two paragraphs — not the television program "law & order."

headline: a wiring war among giants
abstract: article on intensifying turf war between verizon and its rivals, comcast and cablevision, for television service across new york metropolitan area; verizon is training scores of installation technicians and is spending millions to build state-of-the-art fiber optic network and market 'triple play' bundle of products that can help chip away at cable television's dominance in pay television market; state lawmakers are moving ahead on franchise laws and lawmakers in washington are debating bill that would establish nationwide filing process; photos (l)

headline: hints of a strong economy help stocks
abstract: roundup of last week's stock market activity; graphs (m)

headline: on the run as war crosses another line in africa
abstract: chadian rebels, supported by sudanese government, are using central african republic as staging ground to mount attacks over border into chad, spreading humanitarian crisis; situation is so bad in some places that 50,000 residents have actually fled to refuge in chad, while starvation threatens hundreds of thousands of people who remain; government soldiers have also been burning villages to smoke out homegrown rebel movement; central african republic is one of world's poorest countries and has suffered series of coups and countercoups over past decade; united nations is examining possibility of deploying international troops to protect borders; photos; map (l)

headline: a house divided: uncivil war on e. 73rd
abstract: article details longstanding and acrimonious feud between george pavia, owner of elegant manhattan brownstone on east 73rd street, and tenant james couri; pavia has accused couri of engaging in various forms of 'nuisance' behavior, which he contends undermines his family's and other tenants' rights to peaceful habitation; couri has countersued, contending pavia failed to disclose rent-stabilized status of building; latest dispute is scheduled to be heard in new york state supreme court in february; photos (l)

headline: which economy will guide the fed?
abstract: when it comes to calculating the odds of rate cuts next year, the math no longer seems simple.

headline: correction: sounding an alarm after an idyll is broken
abstract: because of an editing error, a column last week on residents in darien and rowayton who do not want trucks to use route 136 as a shortcut to interstate 95 misstated the purpose of a petition by the group. the petition is for trucks to stop using route 136, not interstate 95.

headline: correction: the gridler’s tale
abstract: an essay last sunday about bicycling through queens misidentified an attraction of the 1939-40 world's fair, held at the site now known as flushing meadows-corona park. it was the trylon, not the pylon.

headline: in tsunami’s wake, old foes in war now wage politics
abstract: tsunami that killed 170,000 people and left half million homeless in indonesia's aceh province seems to have taken fire out of 29-year conflict between government and separatist rebels; hard-won peace agreement that made election possible appears to be holding; if process continues to move forward, armed insurgency group will perform rare feat of transforming itself into political party within government it opposed; photos (m)

headline: war of words in new jersey on tax relief
abstract: new jersey gov jon s corzine requests that state legislature consider changing state's pension and health benefits system as one way to reduce high property taxes; corzine had initially asked state senate president richard j codey and assembly speaker joseph j roberts jr to leave any such changes for union contract negotiations, but now says that he will 'respectfully and objectively' evaluate merits of legislative proposal (m)

headline: iraq is failing to spend billions in oil revenues
abstract: iraq is not spending billions of dollars of oil revenues set aside to rebuild its damaged roads, schools and power stations and to repair refineries and pipelines, even as american financial support dwindles; bureaucrats are so fearful and confused by anticorruption measures put in place by american and iraqi governments that they are afraid to sign off on contracts; inability to spend money raises serious questions for government; it has to demonstrate to citizens who are skeptical and suspicious of government corruption that it can improve basic services, and that as american funds are being reduced it can prove to other foreign donors that it can quickly put to use money they may be willing to commit; photo (m)

headline: u.s. rebukes china on trade ahead of paulson trip
abstract: the bush administration accused china today of failing to meet commitments to the world trade organization.

headline: bush capitulates to reality in the middle east
abstract: us president george w. bush doesn't have much time to implement a change in strategy in iraq. and anything he does is likely to be questioned in the middle east. reactions from the region have been full of skepticism.      last wednesday, the day the iraq study group report on us involvement in iraq was released, three blue cars, all opel vectras, separated from the early morning traffic at the al-qadisiyah highway interchange in baghdad and forced a red mercedes to the side of the road. young men wearing flip-flops and tracksuits, their faces wrapped in palestinian scarves, got out, clicked off the safeties on their kalashnikovs and moved toward the mercedes. traffic came to a halt.

headline: rights group urges china to end curbs on lawyers
abstract: a new report said rules requiring chinese lawyers to submit to government supervision in politically delicate cases should be rescinded.

headline: bidding war for steelmaker escalates
abstract: attempts by competing indian and brazilian steelmakers to acquire the anglo-dutch steel producer corus group developed into a full-fledged bidding war today.

headline: china moves to open banking sector to foreign competition
abstract: china’s banking regulator said it had received eight applications from foreign banks for local registration, which it would begin processing on monday, a first step in granting national treatment. the mainland issued new foreign bank guidelines on november 16 to fulfill its obligations for entry into the world trade organization, which stipulates that the country must further open its banking sector to overseas competition from december 11.

headline: the war at home: dueling strategies
abstract: leaders of the iraq study group tried to play nice with the white house on sunday by acknowledging that democracy remains a goal, rather than sticking to more moderate language about an iraq that can govern itself.

headline: venture bubble redux? not by this math
abstract: the foreboding headline on a financial times story monday is not sitting well with at least one venture investor. “vc rises to dotcom bubble levels,” the headline declares. the article goes onto explain that total venture-capital investment is estimated to reach $32 billion this year, which is the highest in the past four years and “closer to levels seen during the dot-com bubble.”

headline: estranged merger partners square off in court
abstract: the chief executive of valassis communications took the stand monday as a trial over his company’s ill-fated $1.3 billion deal to buy advo got underway. valassis, a marketing company, wants to nullify the all-cash merger, contending that advo concealed financial problems; advo argues that valassis is suffering from buyers’ remorse.

headline: s&p sees mergers in health care, chips
abstract: there will likely be “heavy industry m&a activity” in the health care sector next year, particularly among hospitals, according to standard & poor’s ratingdirect’s 2007 outlook. in the hospital sector, “negative trends,” such as slow growth in admissions and rising levels of bad debt, have made “certain hospital groups vulnerable to takeovers by financial buyers, as we saw with the hca leveraged buyout” this year, s&p said.

headline: the war at home: new cbs poll
abstract: cbs news, which regularly partners with the times on polls, has gone solo on an effort largely focused on the iraq war, and surprise, americans’ opinion of president bush’s handling of iraq keeps plummeting.

headline: world business briefing | asia: china: inflation reaches 20-month high
abstract: woø

headline: united and continental discussing possible merger
abstract: united airlines is holding preliminary talks to merge with continental airlines.

headline: texas instruments cuts sales forecast
abstract: sales will be $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion, compared with an october forecast of $3.46 billion to $3.75 billion, because of lower revenue from handsets.

headline: before visit to china, a rebuke
abstract: bush administration, in rebuke to china on eve of high-level visit by american officials, formally accuses chinese leaders of failing to meet commitments to open nation's economy and crack down on piracy of foreign goods; criticism comes in 100-page report to congress by us trade representative susan c schwab; report is required by american law on fifth anniversary of china's joining world trade organization; cites continued limits by china on sales of financial services by foreign banks, including credit cards, and limits on some sales of farm goods; also accuses china of engaging in counterfeiting or piracy of software, videos, pharmaceuticals and other goods, sometimes with open encouragement of chinese officials, and of failing to stiffen punishments on those engaging in these practices; china announces that it will begin to take formal steps to allow foreign banks to offer some retail banking services, like credit cards, and to buy shares in domestic banks; us treas sec henry m paulson jr is expected in china on dec 13; photo (m)

headline: war opponents are convicted in u.n. protest
abstract: cindy sheehan, the antiwar activist, was convicted of trespassing while trying to deliver an antiwar petition last march to united states diplomats at the united nations.

headline: under pressure from moscow, shell offers to sell stake in big oil and gas project
abstract: royal dutch shell offers to sell stake in $20 billion sakhalin island project to gazprom, giving in to pressure of kremlin's campaign to tighten control over oil industry; government-owned gazprom seeks control over gas supplies to asia similar to its monopoly over supplies to europe (m)

headline: huge profit at goldman brings big bonuses
abstract: $16.5 billion was set aside for salaries, bonuses and benefits, or an average of $622,000 for each employee.

headline: google to issue transferable stock options
abstract: the move will enable google's employees to earn more money from stock options.

headline: merger to create word’s largest zinc producer
abstract: zinifex and umicore agreed to combine their zinc smelters and sell shares in what would be the world’s largest producer of the metal. zinifex, based in melbourne, australia, will contribute 60 percent of the assets and umicore, of brussels, 40 percent. zinifex’s smelters may be worth 1.26 billion australian dollars ($990 million), according to abn amro estimates.

headline: is claire’s deal a bubble benchmark?
abstract: the share price of claire’s stores, the jewelry retailer, climbed 4.3 percent on monday as investors continued to speculate on a possible buyout. in the latest installment, women’s wear daily said monday that the bidding for the retailer, which has struggled in recent months to keep up its growth, has entered its second round, with four firms bidding about $39 a share. but despite the feeding frenzy, one analyst sees the marks of a private equity bubble in such a deal.

headline: white house to delay shift on iraq until ’07
abstract: officials suggested that the president’s advisers were locked in internal debates on several fronts about how to proceed in iraq.

headline: google to offer variation on stock options
abstract: google, in move that will enable its employees to earn more money from stock options, says it will create system allowing options to be sold as well as expected; google will grant employees new type of option, called transferable stock option; company will work with morgan stanley to set up market that will enable financial institutions and other investors to bid for those options (m)

abstract: a taker of 25% of

headline: visions of bonus heaven in goldman sachs profit
abstract: quarterly profits soared 93 percent, and the bank is paying $16.5 billion in compensation this year, roughly $623,418 per employee.

headline: world briefing | europe: russia: police raid office of garry kasparov
abstract: garry kasparov says russian counter-terrorist police raided the offices of political organization founded by him, and seized books and printed materials promoting march against president vladimir v putin; photo (s)

headline: the fed leaves short-term rates alone
abstract: the federal reserve warned that inflation remained a concern, offering little hope that it would cut rates early next year.

headline: russia: police raid office of garry kasparov
abstract: counter-terrorist police officers raided the offices of a political organization headed by garry kasparov, left, the former world chess champion, and seized books and printed materials promoting a march on saturday against president vladimir v. putin, according to news reports and mr. kasparov. no one was arrested and no charges were filed in the raid, which lasted more than an hour in the organization’s moscow headquarters. mr. kasparov, who retired from professional chess last year to form the organization, united civil front, said in a telephone interview that the search was unlawful. “we’re talking about the putin regime destroying our country,” he said, describing the content of the materials seized. “obviously it is unacceptable to this regime.”.

headline: executives urge action to cut dependence on foreign oil
abstract: more than dozen prominent business executives and retired military officers, including fedex chairman frederick w smith and gen p x kelley, retired commandant of marines, are lobbying congress and bush administration to undertake comprehensive campaign to reduce reliance on imported oil; group wants much tougher fuel economy standards, not only on cars and sport utility vehicles, but also on heavy trucks, which some of companies use; they want increased drilling offshore and within us, much harder push for ethanol and other biofuels, and other changes that would permanently reduce importance of oil as strategic commodity and economic force; group, called energy security leadership council, hopes that evidence of broad support from business and military leaders will add weight needed to get its proposals adopted; photo (m)

headline: gazprom seeks 50% of shell gas and oil project
abstract: after months of pressure from russian regulators, shell offered to sell a stake in its oil and gas development to gazprom.

headline: circumcision reduces risk of aids, study finds
abstract: aids experts immediately hailed the result of the study by the national institutes of health, saying it gave the world a new way to fight the spread of aids.

headline: world business briefing | europe: britain: real estate agency acquired
abstract: countrywide agrees to be acquired by 3i group in $1.8 billion deal that takes britain's largest real estate agent private (s)

headline: profit up 93% at goldman
abstract: goldman sachs reported a 93 percent rise in quarterly profits, dropping jaws on wall street and setting a record for an american investment bank.    business day, page c1

headline: airline industry buzzes with merger talk
abstract: fasten your seatbelts: deal discussions in the airline industry are moving into high gear. united airlines and continental airlines have been holding talks on a potential merger, a combination that would create the biggest domestic airline, with an overall value of $9 billion, people involved in the negotiations told the new york times late tuesday. on wednesday, airtran holdings, the parent company of a low-cost carrier that competes with delta air lines, offered to buy the midwest air group for $11.25 a share in cash, or about $290 million.

headline: autostrade abandons $18 billion merger with spanish rival
abstract: autostrade, italy’s biggest toll-road operator, abandoned a 13.6 billion euro ($18 billion) merger with spain’s abertis infraestructuras because of government opposition. “the decision taken by the two companies’ boards is based on their evaluation of the material obstacles preventing completion of the merger,” autostrade said wednesday. lack of italian government approval and demands for a review of road concessions led to the decision, it said. the european commission and italian government have wrangled for five months over italy’s efforts to protect autostrade from a foreign takeover.

headline: anadarko sells more oil assets
abstract: anadarko said tuesday it would sell off additional oil-field assets valued at up to $9 billion and might create a separate partnership for its pipeline holdings as part of a sweeping plan to raise cash to pay down debts. among the properties going on the block are projects in northern louisiana, west texas and in the northern rockies, a stake in a deep-water field in the gulf of mexico and all the firm’s assets in venezuela, anadarko executives told analysts during a presentation at the company’s headquarters in the woodlands.

headline: new york board of trade members green light merger
abstract: the members of the new york board of trade late monday approved the $1 billion-plus merger by the intercontinental exchange in a move that clears the way for the upstart electronic exchange to buy the 136-year-old center for open-outcry commodities trading. the new york board of trade said 93 percent of the votes cast were in favor of the merger.

headline: a taker for 25% of russia’s phone company
abstract: it didn’t take the financier george soros long to declare his 1997 bet on russia’s national telephone company the worst investment of his career. in a new twist to the long and fraught history of this investment, an up-and-coming telecommunications company on tuesday snapped up 25 percent of the company, svyazinvest, for $1.3 billion, signaling the intense interest these days in companies providing services to the growing middle class of russia.

headline: china coal fires up $1.6 billion i.p.o., report says
abstract: china coal energy, one of the nation’s largest coal producers, raised 13.16 billion hong kong dollars ($1.69 billion) in its initial public offering after fund managers ordered more than 35 times the stock on offer, bloomberg news said. china coal sold 3.25 billion shares, or a 28.9 percent stake, at 4.05 hong kong dollars each, according to the report.

headline: 3i buys largest real estate chain in britain
abstract: a london buyout shop, the 3i group, bid 940.7 million pounds ($1.8 billion) in cash and stock for the largest chain of real estate agents in britain, countrywide. the offer, announced after the london stock exchange closed tuesday, values each countrywide share at 550.6 pence.

headline: the war at home: patience, patience
abstract: don’t expect to hear anything from president bush on a new iraq strategy until early 2007, but you just might hear about sending more troops.

headline: a great google plan
abstract: google’s options plan offers good news for employees — and shareholders.

headline: monster worldwide restates 9 years of earnings
abstract: the owner of the most used online job-listing service reduced past earnings by $271.9 million to correct stock-based compensation costs.

headline: circumcision halves h.i.v. risk, u.s. agency finds
abstract: national institutes of health says circumcision appears to reduce man's risk of contracting aids from heterosexual sex by half; nih halts two clinical trials in kenya and uganda, saying that not offering circumcision to all men taking part would be unethical; aids experts hail finding but caution that circumcision only lessens chances that man will catch virus and should be used with other prevention methods; they say procedure is expensive and has serious risks if performed under unsanitary conditions, as often happens in rural africa; two largest funds for fighting aids say they will consider paying for circumcisions in high-risk countries (m)

headline: somalia’s islamists and ethiopia gird for a war
abstract: islamists in control of mogadishu, somalia, prepare for war with ethiopia, which would further destabilize troubled horn of africa; ethiopia, with tacit approval from us, has been assembling troops to try to hold off islamists and shore up somalia's weak, unpopular transitional government; analysts unanimously agree that full-scale conflict between islamists and ethiopia would be disastrous for somalia and for entire region, because neighboring countries might join war; some analysts say us and united nations approach misreads islamists' power, rooted not in military strength but in their widespread popular support; they say ethiopia may have strongest military in region, but attacking islamist forces may only drive them underground, into guerrilla insurgency; map; photos (m)

headline: opec calls for 2nd cut in oil output
abstract: the decision was the strongest signal yet that opec aims to keep oil prices above $60 a barrel next year.

headline: iranian election is seen as test of public view of president
abstract: iranians to vote in dec 15 elections for city councils and 86-member assembly of experts that are seen as test of whether pres mahmoud ahmadinejad still has popular support that led to his victory 18 months ago; in tehran city elections, slate affiliated with ahmadinejad is running against other radicals who have been sidelined by him and against reformist politicians trying to make comeback; analysts say opposing group has chance of winning if turnout is low; notes ahmadinejad's uncompromising position on iran's nuclear program has caused country to face possible sanctions; say he has also failed to deliver on his promise of improving people's economic status (m)

headline: home depot to buy protégé retailer in china
abstract: home depot is buying homeway, a move that will give the chain its first stores in the fast-growing chinese market.

headline: u.s. hits resistance at economic talks in china
abstract: treasury secretary henry paulson is leading an elaborate effort to persuade china to reform its policies.

headline: agency cuts atlantic yards revenue estimate
abstract: the change represents a drop of one-third, or nearly half a billion dollars, from the estimate the development agency released in july.

headline: settlements including fines are reached in election finance cases of three groups
abstract: the federal election commission announced that it had reached settlements with three 527 groups, including the swift boat veterans for truth.

headline: china tries rights lawyer, barring his kin and counsel
abstract: gao zhisheng, outspoken chinese human rights lawyer, is put on trial in beijing, accused of inciting subversion; his lawyer claims authorities are preventing him and gao's family from attending; gao is one of most well-known dissidents in china; his lacerating essays on internet have included predictions that governing communist party will implode because of corruption and abuse of power; he has taken on cases other chinese lawyers would not dare touch, including representing advocates of banned falun gong sect; photo (m)

headline: in russia, mixed signals on search for radiation
abstract: a russian agency said it would search planes in the inquiry over alexander v. litvinenko. but officials at the state-controlled airline said the agency had refused.

headline: russia cancels iran talks after u.s. comment on belarus
abstract: a summary of the top stories in russian newspapers on thursday.    top stories    vedomosti    belarus comment disrupts u.n.-iran talks: the united states provoked a diplomatic scandal with russia on wednesday by bringing up the issue of belarus's political situation during a session of the united nations security council on lebanon and the ivory coast. russia's representative called off a scheduled session to review a resolution on sanctions against iran later in the day after his american counterpart voiced concern over the health of aleksandr kozulin, a belarusian opposition leader jailed for five and a half years for his participation in antigovernment protests. also on tuesday, the united states senate passed a resolution calling on the president to impose sanctions against belarus.    kommersant    deputies call for health minister's ouster: a group of duma deputies from united russia on wednesday called for the suspension and eventual removal of mikhail y. zurabov, the minister of health and social development, following a recent corruption scandal associated with his ministry. the director and deputy director of the compulsory medical insurance fund, which falls under mr. zurabov's ministry, were arrested in november and charged with bribe-taking and misappropriation of funds. since president vladimir v. putin has already voiced his approval of mr. zurabov's work, however, members of the opposition said they doubted he would be fired.    nezavisimaya gazeta    france closes borders to russian tourists: the french embassy in moscow stopped issuing visas on tuesday to russian citizens planning on european bus tours during the holidays. the embassy said an unprecedented number of visa requests from russians booking in bus toursforced it to curb its document processing. tour operators, meanwhile, have called on the russian foreign ministry to intervene in the situation.    izvestia    litvinenko witness poisoned earlier than suspected: dmitri v. kovtun, who, along with alexander v. litvinenko, a former russian intelligence officer, was contaminated with the radioactive isotope, polonium 210, announced on wednesday that he was likely poisoned in mid-october and not on nov. 1 as originally suspected. according to the newspaper, mr. kovtun's statement lends more credence to the theory that he, together with mr. litvinenko and andrei k. lugovoi, who was also contaminated, were engaged in some kind of polonium project directed by boris a. berezovsky, the london-based russian émigré acquainted with all three. whether they desired to export the radioactive substance to the middle east or build a dirty bomb is up to scotland yard to figure out, the newspaper said.    gazeta    maria versus darwin: judges in st. petersburg on wednesday postponed a final decision on russia's first ever lawsuit challenging the teaching of the theory of evolution in public schools. maria shreiber, a 16-year-old middle school student, filed the suit after declaring her school's biology curriculum violated her rights as a religious believer. the case has had nationwide resonance, prompting calls of support from religious groups and sparking debates in the state duma.    british ambassador blames kremlin for harassment: britain's ambassador to russia on tuesday accused the kremlin of backing the actions of the pro-government youth organization, nashi, which has waged a four-month harassment campaign against the diplomat. nashi leaders have accused anthony brenton of supporting a ''fascist gathering'' after his participation in an anti-kremlin, liberal-opposition conference in moscow in july. britain has angered the russian government by repeatedly ignoring russian requests to extradite suspected criminals and by frequently criticizing kremlin policies.    vremya novostei    secretary's suspension shows rift in chechen leadership: a court in chechnya on wednesday approved the suspension of the government compensation agency secretary, accused by the prosecutor's office of taking bribes from civilians seeking payment for wartime losses. chechnya's prime minister, ramzan a. kadyrov, who heads the agency, has from the beginning defended his secretary. the suspension of such a high-ranking chechen official, directly associated with the prime minister, the newspaper said, pointed to the mutual dissatisfaction of federal law enforcement and mr. kadyrov with one another, a trend both sides have tried to keep out of public view.    moskovsky komsomolets    a question of holiday tradition: a statue of santa claus that appeared two days ago at the main entrance of the state duma prompted a nationalist outcry over the infiltration of western cultural traditions. deputies promptly had the statue removed and proposed replacing it with a more appropriate representation of the russian grandpa frost. the newspaper, however, pointed out that the two holiday icons are difficult to differentiate and further noted that the decorated tree festooning the duma's entrance was also a western import.

headline: world business briefing | europe: italy: toll-road concerns drop merger
abstract: world b

headline: italy: toll-road concerns drop merger
abstract: autostrade, italy’s biggest toll-road operator, abandoned a 13.6 billion euro ($18 billion) merger with abertis infraestructuras of spain because of italian government opposition. lack of government approval and demands for a review of road concessions led to the decision, autostrade and abertis said in a joint statement. autostrade is based in milan and abertis is based in barcelona. the combination would have created the world’s largest highway operator, with about 6,713 kilometers (4,200 miles) of highways in europe and the united states under management.

headline: mortgage lender hbos to report rise in earnings
abstract: hbos, britain’s biggest mortgage lender, said 2006 profit probably rose more than 11 percent as it tapped a surge in home borrowing. earnings will beat analysts’ median estimate for pretax profit of 5.35 billion pounds ($10.5 billion), or 96.8 pence a share, the bank said thursday.

headline: china everbright bank sells stake ahead of i.p.o.
abstract: china’s central huijin investment won approval to inject at least 15 billion yuan ($1.9 billion) into china everbright bank to strengthen the firm’s balance sheet before an initial public offering, bloomberg news reported. the report said that huijin investment, a state-owned holding company, will become china everbright’s largest shareholder, paving the way for the nation’s eighth-largest bank to sell a stake to strategic investors before an i.p.o. that may raise at least $1 billion next year.

headline: on stock options, google gets creative
abstract: google has long been a maverick when it comes to financial matters. it took a nontraditional approach to its initial public offering, and now, the internet search giant is adopting a novel strategy for dealing with stock options given to employees. like many of google’s moves, the program is drawing a lot of attention, a great deal of praise and a few warnings.

headline: lehman, bear stearns report higher earnings
abstract: for wall street’s top investment banks, the good times continue to roll. only days after goldman sachs reported record fourth-quarter earnings, lehman brothers and bear stearns posted profits thursday that beat analysts’ expectations. bear stearns’ stock was up 1.3 percent in late-morning trading to $158, near ts 52-week high of $160.53. shares of lehman were volatile, trading higher in early dealings and then turning about 1 percent lower.

headline: the war at home: bush won’t be “rushed”
abstract: president bush said that he won’t be “rushed” into deciding on a new strategy for iraq.

headline: criminal inquiries look at u.s. oil-gas unit
abstract: justice department begins two criminal investigations into interior department's minerals management service, which is already focus of several inquiries into its collection of royalties for oil and gas produced on federal property; interior's inspector general earl e devaney says new probes are still in early stages; one justice inquiry involves interior officials in denver who manage government's fast-growing program to collect 'royalties in kind,' which are royalties in form of oil and gas rather than in financial payments; focus of second probe is unclear, but it is being conducted by devaney with help from fbi; word of criminal probes surfaces as interior department announces that bp, conocophillips, marathon oil, royal dutch shell and walter oil and gas voluntarily renegotiated leases and agreed to not exploit loophole that could save them hundreds of millions of dollars each; leases gave companies to drill in deepwater in gulf of mexico by letting them skip royalties on millions of barrels of oil and gas; leases omitted standard escape clause that would have required companies to pay in full if oil prices rose above about $34 per barrel; about 50 other companies have not yet agreed to change their leases; among them is chevron, one of biggest potential beneficiaries of error; photo (m)

headline: white house upset by senator’s trip to syria
abstract: white house says democratic sen bill nelson's meeting with pres bashar al-assad in syria was inappropriate and undermines democracy in region; three more senators, including republican sen arlen specter, make plans to visit damascus in defiance of pres bush; he has steadfastly resisted talks with syria, even after iraq study group calls for such talks; nelson claims he sees 'crack in the door' for us to cooperate with syria on iraq (m)

headline: law firms’ merger will expand reach
abstract: kirkpatrick & lockhart nicholson graham and preston gates & ellis agree to merge to form one of nation's largest law firms with 1,400 lawyers and expected revenue for 2007 of $750 million (m)

headline: world business briefing | asia: china: air china leads shake-up of hong kong airlines
abstract: independent shareholders of china national aviation company accept air china's 3.23 billion hong kong dollars ($416 million) offer for shares it did not already own; raises its stake in cathay pacific airways to 17.5 percent (s)5

headline: rescuers search for american climbers in china
abstract: efforts are focusing on a remote region near tibet where two elite climbers apparently went missing.

headline: world business briefing | europe: poland: oil concern buys a refinery
abstract: pkn orlen buys 53.7 percent of mazeikiu nafta refinery in lithuania for $1.46 billion from yukos; is expected to buy additional 30.6 percent from government for $851 million (s)

headline: debt trading aids earnings of two firms on wall st.
abstract: lehman brothers holdings and the bear stearns companies, the wall street companies most dependent on the fixed-income market, posted record fourth-quarter earnings, helped by corporate bonds and derivatives.

headline: sectarian and ethnic lines in sand stall provision of iraqi oil law
abstract: the law is a crucial step in the process of national reconciliation because it could ease tensions over granting greater autonomy to iraq’s regions.

headline: talks with china end with few signs of progress on currency issue
abstract: top officials from china and united states end two days of economic talks with little progress on american demand that china stop undervaluing its currency to promote exports; treasury secretary henry m paulson jr is optimistic that dialogue will promote progress in future; photo (m)

headline: russia says it will test planes for isotope in poisoning case
abstract: russian government agency says it would test several passenger airplanes for traces of radioactive isotope that killed alexander v litvinenko in london, but officials at state controlled aeroflot say agemcu told them there would be no inspections; contradictory statements underscore uncertain response of russian authorities in murder case that litvinenko, without direct evidence, laid at feet of pres vladimir v putin and country's secretive security services (m)

headline: u.a.w. president won’t rule out a merger with another union
abstract: with membership in the united automobile workers union at its lowest level since world war ii, the president of the u.a.w., ron gettelfinger, left open the possibility on thursday of a merger with another union.     during a question-and-answer session on the u.a.w. web site, mr. gettelfinger was asked if he foresaw a merger, a move that would help the union regain some of the influence it has lost as hundreds of thousands of factory jobs have been eliminated.

headline: hint of shift in white house kitchen
abstract: a new york pastry chef appears ready to make a permanent change in his place of employment — to 1600 pennsylvania avenue.

headline: eurotunnel bondholders approve debt plan
abstract: eurotunnel, operator of the tunnel linking britain and france, moved closer to exiting bankruptcy protection thursday when its bondholders, including deutsche bank, approved the company’s plan to cut its 6.2 billion pounds ($12.1 billion) of debt.

headline: malaysian acquisition by wilmar creates asian palm oil giant
abstract: shares of wilmar international surged as much as 27 percent after its chairman, a nephew of a malaysian billionaire, robert kuok, offered to pool the family’s palm-oil assets to create the world’s largest oilseed refiner.

headline: cisco injects $50 million into china communications
abstract: cisco systems announced a $50 million investment in the newly public china communications services, making the cmopany the largest foreign investor in china communications. formerly a subsidiary of the state-controlled china telecom group, china communications went public earlier this month on the hong kong stock exchange. china telecom, china mobile and china unicom are the other big investors in china communications.

headline: u.s. regulators move to streamline merger reviews
abstract: hoping to reduce the time and expense involved in the merger review process, the justice department’s antitrust division on friday announced changes to its five-year-old guidelines for vetting corporate transactions. many of the changes focus on the “second request,” in which regulators, after launching a preliminary investigation into a deal’s competitive effects, extend the waiting period and ask the parties for more information. among the new provisions is an option that allows companies to limit the scope of the documents they must produce in a second request, the justice department said.

headline: chief says credit suisse doesn’t need a deal
abstract: credit suisse might be a tempting takeover candidate, but the economist concludes that switzerland’s second-biggest bank (after ubs) would fight off any such attempt. on the subject of credit suisse as target, oswald grübel, the firm’s chief executive, “dismisses that idea with a puff of cigar smoke,” the magazine says. mr. grubel “seems in no mood to surrender command,” according to the economist, though at 63, he is a year past the bank’s official retirement age for board members.

headline: close, but no gold for iraq
abstract: qatar defeats iraq for the gold in asian games…

headline: tools for a war zone: the bible and a teddy bear
abstract: the rev. shareen fischer, one of only 52 female chaplains on active duty in the army, is preparing to deploy with 470 soldiers to afghanistan.

headline: search is on for 2 american mountaineers missing in a little-traveled part of china
abstract: search efforts are focusing on a remote region near tibet where the two americans apparently wanted to climb two isolated mountains.

headline: latest consumer price data ease fears of inflation
abstract: the latest report showed that inflation was following an arc that must give some relief to the federal reserve.

headline: hazardous inlet makes fuel oil delivery perilous
abstract: port for long island sound captain peter boynton says spill of heating oil and diesel fuel into east rockaway inlet at reynolds channel may have been averted only because of multi-agency effort to refloat tanker kristin poling, which ran aground in inlet on november 17; gary cutler, an owner, says poling & cutler is considering dropping route because it is too hazardous; photo (m)

headline: in a merger wave, a dangerous undertow for stocks
abstract: the correlation between stock market tops and soaring mergers and acquisitions levels is no coincidence.

headline: eli lilly said to play down risk of top pill
abstract: internal company documents suggest eli lilly has engaged in effort since 1999 to downplay health risks of its best-selling schizophrenia medication zyprexa, which data link to obesity and elevated blood sugar, both known risk factors for diabetes; zyprexa had sales of $4.2 billion in 2005, when about two million people worldwide took drug; documents were collected as part of lawsuits on behalf of mentally ill people against lilly and are replete with references to zyprexa's importance to lilly's future and need to keep concerns about weight and diabetes from hurting sales; photos (l)

headline: first civil  war
abstract: william safire column on differences over whether violence in iraq rises to level of civil war or should be called something else, such as insurgency or sectarian strife (m)

headline: new highs for indexes, and no move by the fed
abstract: the dow jones industrial average and the standard & poor’s 500-stock index on friday both reached all-time closing highs.

headline: databank; new highs for indexes, and no move by the fed
abstract: roundup of past week's stock market results; graphs (m)2

headline: iraq’s legal system staggers beneath the weight of war
abstract: the system in iraq for detaining, charging and trying suspects has become another weak link in the rule of law.

headline: new to russia, google struggles to find its footing
abstract: google, bedeviled in russia by cultural and language issues, trails local internet companies in both executing searches and collecting rubles on related ads.

headline: stock market offerings scheduled for this week
abstract: the following equity and convertible debt offerings are expected this week:     artes medical, an initial public offering of 4.6 million shares. cowen and lazard freres.  claymont steel holdings, an initial public offering of 6.3 million shares. jefferies.  dayton superior, an initial public offering of 7.9 million shares. robert w. baird.  freedom acquisition holdings, 37.5 million units, representing one common share and one warrant. citigroup.  fuwel films holdings (china), an initial public offering of 3.8 million shares. maxim.  hospitality properties trust, 12 million common shares of beneficial interest. merrill lynch, morgan stanley, rbc capital markets, ubs and wachovia.  melco pbl entertainment (macau) limited, an initial public offering of 53 million american depositary shares, each representing three ordinary shares. credit suisse, citigroup and ubs.  oculus innovative sciences, an initial public offering of 3.1 million shares. roth.  solarfun power holdings (china), an initial public offering of 12 million american depositary shares, each representing five ordinary shares. goldman sachs.  supertel hospitality, seven million shares. robert w. baird.  trina solar limited (china), an initial public offering of 5.3 million american depositary shares, each representing one ordinary share. merrill lynch.  valero g. p. holdings., 17.9 million units representing limited liability company interests. lehman brothers, ubs, citigroup and morgan stanley.  wet seal, 16 million class a shares. credit suisse. headline: latest deal in real estate for $9 billion
abstract: realogy, the giant real estate franchisor, agreed sunday to be sold to apollo group, the private equity firm, for about $9 billion.

headline: from heavy metal to symphonic rock and holiday gold
abstract: the band trans-siberian orchestra has sold five million copies of its christmas rock operas over the last decade, as its elaborate, effects-filled shows have packed u.s. arenas.

headline: election seen  as setback for iran’s president
abstract: partial election returns suggested that president mahmoud ahmadinejad had experienced a major setback barely over a year after his own election.

headline: blessed by a u.s. official, china will buy 4 nuclear reactors
abstract: the deal may stir worries in washington that the united states is selling its competitive advantage an industry at a time.

headline: apple delays earnings statement due to options grants
abstract: apple computer, the maker of ipod music players, delayed filing its financial statements on friday for the second time, and said it would restate earnings to account for backdated stock-option grants. the size of any charge related to the options has not been finalized. apple, based in cupertino, california, said it now planned to file its quarterly and annual reports with regulators by dec. 29. this is the first confirmation that apple will restate its results because of the grants. previously, the company, also the maker of macintosh computers, had said only that a revision might be necessary.

headline: apollo leads latest deal in real estate for $9 billion
abstract: realogy, the giant real estate franchisor that owns coldwell banker, century 21 and sotheby’s international realty agreed sunday to be sold to apollo group, the private equity firm, for about $9 billion. the deal marks the latest play by private equity firms to buy into the real estate business just as it appears to have peaked.

headline: the war at home: day 1
abstract: today is robert m. gates’s first as secretary of defense.

headline: valassis and advo in talks to settle merger litigation
abstract: the trial over the proposed merger between valassis communications and advo was halted for a day after the two sides that they had entered into settlement talks. the discussions were announced monday in a joint press release, which said there was no guarantee a settlement would be reached. valassis, a marketing company, has asked the court to nullify its all-cash $1.3 billion merger with advo, contending that advo hid its financial problems. advo wants the deal to proceed, arguing that valassis is simply suffering from buyers’ remorse. the trial began a week ago in delaware’s court of chancery.

headline: focus on the middle east
abstract: alison smale, managing editor of the international herald tribune, discusses recent events in the middle east.

headline: a choice of tenses in war of words
abstract: perhaps the touchiest subject of all is whether the united states is winning or losing the war in iraq.

headline: express scripts set to fight a proxy war for caremark
abstract: express scripts is willing to engage in a proxy war to acquire caremark rx and break up the merger of caremark and cvs.

headline: overhaul moves white house data center into modern era
abstract: white house situation room is to re-open after completing biggest high-tech overhaul of computers and telephones since its creation during cuban missile crisis in early 1960's; photos (m)

headline: group plans to build china-u.s. fiber optic link
abstract: verizon communications unit and consortium of five asian companies, including china telecom, china netcom, china unicom, korea telecom and chunghwa telecom, agree to build high-speed fiber optic cable to link china and united states before olympic games open in beijing in august 2008; construction of 11,000 mile cable will cost $500 million; will end by third quarter of 2008 (m)

headline: ebay is expected to close its auction site in china
abstract: ebay will shut its main web site in china and enter into joint venture with tom online inc, internet company based in beijing; ebay will take 49 percent stake in venture, taking majority share and administering venture, which has yet to be named; plans call for ebay to put $40 million into venture and tom online to contribute $20 million (m)

headline: 2 sides in disputed merger hold talks
abstract: a trial over valassis communications' attempt to cancel its $1.9 billion acquisition of advo inc. was stopped yesterday so the companies could pursue settlement talks.      vice chancellor leo e. strine jr. in chancery court in wilmington, del., canceled what would have been the sixth day of testimony in the trial over valassis's claim that it was misled by advo's financial projections. the trial may resume today if the parties cannot agree.

headline: china tightens adoption rules, u.s. agencies say
abstract: the new regulations seem certain to slow the rapid rise in applications by foreign parents to adopt chinese babies.

headline: with nasa, google expands its realm to the moon and mars
abstract: nasa ames research center and google inc will collaborate on projects to make space and weather data widely available on internet; say initiative will bring 'excitement of space travel' to wider audience; may develop products like google earth to view three-dimensional images of moon and other planets; specific terms of agreement are not discussed (m)

headline: economic report provides reminder on inflation
abstract: the producer price index rose 2 percent in november, the highest increase in more than 32 years.

headline: french utility merger may be stalled, report says
abstract: gaz de france and the franco-belgian utility suez appeared to admit defeat in their race to merge before the french presidential election, dealing a blow to the french government’s ambition to create a gallic energy champion, the times of london reported. the newspaper, citing an anonymous source, said both groups agreed that it would be “difficult” to ask shareholders to vote on the 80-billion-euro tie-up before next july. with the french presidential election due in april, the outcome of the merger is effectively in the hands of the electorate.

headline: ebay to close china office and partner up, reports say
abstract: ebay, acknowledging that the online auction market in china is enticingly fast-growing but frustratingly tough to crack, will shut its main web site in china and enter into a joint venture with a chinese company instead, according to press reports.

headline: euronext shareholders approve nyse merger
abstract: euronext shareholders on tuesday overwhelmingly approved the exchange’s $14 billion merger with nyse group, lifting one of the final hurdles to completing the first transatlantic exchange merger. around 98.2 percent of shareholders present or represented at the meeting backed the merger deal, with 1.8 percent voting against.

headline: the war at home: coming and going
abstract: the white house wants to send more troops to iraq. the joint chiefs of staff don’t.

headline: panic in thailand
abstract: a plunge in thailand’s stock market shows how rapidly capital can flee.

headline: china tightens adoption rules for foreigners
abstract: china plans to tighten its restrictions on foreign adoptions, barring people who are single, obese, older than 50 or who fail to meet certain benchmarks in financial, physical or psychological health from adopting chinese children, according to adoption agencies in the united states.

headline: on a military base, comfort for students whose parents are at war
abstract: education column on mcnair elementary school at fort bragg, nc, military base, where about one-third of 350 students have parent on active military duty overseas; principal timothy howle, veteran of army's special forces, says biggest challenge is making children feel that school is a constant and that it is 'a safe place, a home'; some of projects used to comfort students described; photo (m) displaying arrays of parents' photographs and sending packages and letters overseas; photo (m)

abstract: labor department reportsã

abstract: thailand's central bank imposes capital controls to lower value of nation's currency after one-day plunge of 15 percent in country's stock market; photo (m)

headline: thai stock market rebounds from plunge
abstract: the decline of the dollar is punishing asia’s smaller economies, the governor of the thai central bank said today.

headline: google steps more boldly into paypal’s territory
abstract: google is getting thousands of customers to sign up for its new payment service google checkout; google is not charging merchants any processing fees through end of 2007; many customers are placing ads alongside google's search results, exactly what google wants; checkout was seen as formidable rival to ebay's paypal online payment service when it was introduced in june; checkout's use with some merchants has already surpassed paypal's; service is calculated effort to expand google's base of advertisers, which provide bulk of company's revenues; steve grossberg, who sells video games online and uses checkout, comments; photos (m)

headline: white house defends not disclosing first lady’s skin cancer
abstract: the white house press secretary, tony snow, said that laura bush had a right to privacy because she was not a public official.

headline: profit at palm fell by 95% in quarter
abstract: a delay in the release of its newest treo device prompted the first drop in sales at palm inc. in more than three years.

headline: report on china is notably softer on currency valuation
abstract: tuesday’s report said the chinese had made strides in revaluing their currency, but that the progress was “considerably less than is needed.”

headline: fear and hope in immigrant’s furtive existence
abstract: second article in series three sisters describes furtive life of mexican woman named veronica, who lives illegally with husband and four children in san antonio, and fears constantly that she and husband will be arrested and deported back to mexico; her life is far different from that of sister raquel rodriguez, legal immigrant who works and raises family ten miles away, while helping her numerous relatives as much as she can; photos (m)

headline: west increasingly forthright in criticizing russia
abstract: a summary of the top stories in russian newspapers on wednesday.

headline: advising china
abstract: in this lesson, students will consider how an economic boom has affected china and role-play in a letter writing activity.

headline: ebay confirms china move
abstract: ebay confirmed yesterday that it will close its unprofitable china web auction unit and form a venture with billionaire li ka-shing’s tom online to run the business in the world’s second-biggest internet market.

headline: the war at home: ‘not winning’
abstract: “we’re not winning, we’re not losing,” president bush said yesterday.

headline: nyse shareholders approve euronext merger
abstract: the new york stock exchange said wednesday that its shareholders overwhelmingly approved a planned $14.3 billion acquisition of paris-based euronext in a deal that would create the first trans-atlantic financial market. on tuesday, euronext’s shareholders voted in favor of the transaction. the votes set the stage for the nyse euronext to receive final regulatory approval early next year to become the world’s largest stock market.

headline: caremark chief to take reduced payout in merger
abstract: how much does caremark rx chief executive e. mac crawford want his company’s $26 billion deal with cvs to go through? here is one measure: mr. crawford has agreed to accept a reduced cash severance payment of $26.4 million upon his resignation, rather than the $36 million to $40.8 million to which he would normally be entitled.

headline: russia: kremlin sees more spies
abstract: president vladimir v. putin said foreign spies in russia had been “showing heightened interest in classified economic information,” the latest kremlin expression of its worry that it has been under a growing threat from outside intelligence services. mr. putin’s remarks, made on security services day, followed public comments tuesday by nikolai p. patrushev, the head of the domestic intelligence agency, who said foreign news media bureaus were increasingly being used by spies. public hand-wringing about spies has been used to justify crackdowns against groups or classes the kremlin deems as threats, including foreign nongovernmental organizations, whose activities were restricted and more closely regulated with a new law that took effect this year.

headline: gold coins will feature presidential wives
abstract: united states mint is issuing new series of half-ounce pure gold coins which will show all former first ladies in order in which their husbands served; series, officially called first spouses, is first long-running series of us coins devoted to women; coins will not circulate and will number 40,000 each; drawing (m)

headline: a new phrase enters washington’s war of words over iraq
abstract: pres bush and other members of administration are quoting gen peter pace's characterization of war in iraq, 'we are not winning, but we are not losing,' as latest catchphrase to define progress or lack of progress to a public that was promised swift and conclusive end to war; photos (m)

headline: world briefing | europe: russia: kremlin sees more spies
abstract: president vladimir v putin says foreign spies in russia are highly interested in classified information and he is worried that russia is under growing threat from outside intelligence services (s)

headline: congressman criticizes election of muslim
abstract: representative virgil h. goode jr. warned that the election of the first muslim to congress posed a threat to the nation’s traditional values.

headline: the cautious u.s. boom in oil shale
abstract: shell oil, chevron and little-known private texas company named egl resources are experimenting and planning to process organic material in shale into form of oil so it can be pumped to surface; bush administration last month opened up five large parcels of land in piceance creek basin in colorado for oil shale research and development projects; egl resources oil shale projects manager r glenn vawter will begin pilot tests early in 2007; government estimates of recoverable shale oil in colorado, utah and wyoming put reserves at 800 billion barrels; rand corp estimates size of oil resource in three states to range from 1.5 trillion to 1.8 trillion barrels, vastly more than proven oil reserves of saudi arabia; map; photos (l)

headline: bed bath & beyond posts higher profit
abstract: the home furnishings retailer said third-quarter profit rose 5.8 percent, helped by lower purchasing costs for some products.

headline: fedex’s quarterly profit rises 8.5%, but fuel costs put damper on outlook
abstract: fedex reports second-quarter profit rose 8.5 percent due to global demand; net income increased to $511 million in three months that ended november 30, from $471 million year earlier; sales climbed 10 percent, to $8.93 billion (m)

headline: carlyle in  deal for china bank stake
abstract: carlyle group, the biggest u.s. buyout firm, and dah sing financial group agreed to pay 1.01 billion yuan ($129 million) for a combined 25 percent of chongqing city commercial bank to profit from growing demand for financial services in china’s most populous city.

headline: rosie: so sue me! trump: o.k.!
abstract: rosie insults donald. donald insults rosie. discuss…

headline: bickering saudis struggle for an answer to iran’s rising influence in the middle east
abstract: debate in saudi arabia about iran's influence in middle east bursts into open with abrupt resignation of prince turki al-faisal, saudi ambassador to washington; resignation is seen by many as part of long-running battle over saudi arabia's foreign policy; privately, some saudi officials and analysts say prince turki resigned over deep differences with prince bandar bin sultan over how to deal with iran; little is known about his successor adel al-jubeir, although saudi officials say jubeir does not necessarily share prince bandar's opinions; photos (m)

headline: for ebay, it’s about political connections in china
abstract: ebay's decision to close its web site in china and take 49 percent stake in e-commerce venture with china's tom online inc is latest sign that local knowledge and connections matter in chinese market; no one questions that tom online knows chinese market and has political influence; tom online's reliance on wireless services has prompted some experts to question how it will fare in electronic commerce; tom online has political connections that remain crucial in china; li kashing, hong kong's wealthiest tycoon and man who has cultivated close relationships with top communist leaders on mainland for decades, controls company; wang lei lei, chief executive of tom online and chief executive of joint venture, is grandson of people's liberation army general and known for his political connections; photo (m)

headline: thai stocks and currency reflect an ebb in confidence
abstract: thai financial markets resume downward slide as investor concern grows over government's financial policies; prime min surayud chulanont says he supports central bank's imposition of capital controls, which were later lifted (m)

headline: incentives on oil barely help u.s., study suggests
abstract: study finds that federal incentives to encourage offshore drilling in gulf of mexico can cost government billions of dollars in uncollected royalties, yet cause only small increase in production; study also suggests that cost of any additional oil could be as much as $80 a barrel, far more than government would have to pay if it simply bought oil on its own; industry analysts say united states is much more generous to oil companies than most other countries, demanding smaller share of revenues than others that let private companies drill on public lands and in public waters; they note also that while us has sweetened incentives in recent years, dozens of other countries have demanded bigger share of revenue; interior dept, which conducted study, refused to release it for more than year; photos; chart (l)

headline: higher sales bolster profit at general mills
abstract: hed: higher sales bolster profit at general mills.

headline: u.s. to require more security at high-risk chemical plants
abstract: bush administration will move to require security enhancements at high-risk chemical plants nationwide so their hazardous stockpiles do not become terrorist targets; draft regulations will almost certainly evoke protest from congressional democrats and state officials because they may allow federal pre-emption of conflicting and perhaps more demanding state laws; may also allow homeland security department to recognize as sufficient security measures put in place voluntarily by chemical manufacturers, meaning few changes would be required for many plants; american chemistry council says its members welcome regulations, particularly if they credit security investments already in place; critics call move industry friendly (m)

headline: russia excuses itself in final report on beslan
abstract: a parliamentary commission placed blame for the hundreds of deaths on the chechan-led militants alone.

headline: in this election for comptroller, just 107 votes needed to win
abstract: albany, dec. 31 — the expected resignation of the state comptroller, alan g. hevesi, means that just weeks after his re-election, a new comptroller will be chosen not by the voters but by the 212 members of the state legislature. the strange campaign to succeed him has already begun, just barely under the radar screen.

headline: separated by war, reunited through dna
abstract: angela fillingim meets large group of relatives through efforts of dna reunification project, genetic database that helps match children adopted from war zones with biological families; fillingham was adopted when she was six months old by couple in berkeley, calif, during el salvador's civil war; photos (m)

headline: search for u.s. climbers narrows in china
abstract: the decision came after a tip from a woman who met the pair shortly before they disappeared.

headline: world business briefing | europe: sweden: acquisition by chainsaw maker
abstract: husqvarna agrees to buy gardena holding of germany, maker of garden sprinklers and water pumps, for 730 million euros ($963 million) from industri kapital (s)

headline: eyeing ’08, democrats nurse freshmen at risk
abstract: democrats are planning to fortify the most politically shaky members of congress with committee assignments.

headline: with owners in the dark, stocks go up
abstract: floyd norris column on companies that have done fairly well on stock market since they stopped releasing current financial data; holds not enforcing delisting rules when company is encountering financial problems removes incentive to complete financial filings as rapidly possible; companies discussed include navistar international, krispy kreme and take-two interactive software; graph (m)

headline: russians buy control of oil field
abstract: russia's gazprom acquires controlling share of sakhalin 2, vast energy project in russia's remote far east, after highly publicized campaign of pressure on its foreign operator royal dutch shell; gazprom will pay $7.45 billion; critics of sale call it first effective nationalization of large foreign oil or gas project in russia, which this year surpassed saudi arabia on oil production; pres vladimir v putin announces deal at kremlin meeting with executives from gazprom, shell and japanese trading houses mitsui and mitsubishi, which also own part of project; says russia remains open to energy investment; photo (m)

headline: world business briefing | europe: iceland: central bank raises rate
abstract: iceland's central bank sedlabanki raises benchmark interest rate quarter-point to record 14.25 percent after widening current-account deficit threatens to weaken krona and push up inflation (s)

headline: former winterthur head to stay at credit suisse
abstract: credit suisse ended weeks of speculation by confirming that leonhard fischer, the former head of the its winterthur unit, would remain with the firm. mr. fischer will become chief executive of the swiss group’s europe, middle east and africa region, putting him “firmly in the frame” to succeed oswald grubel, the bank’s chief executive, the financial times reported.

headline: russia approves $4.5 billion bank i.p.o.
abstract: russia’s government approved plans by the country’s second-largest bank vtb to hold an initial public offering next may and promised a decision soon on plans by the largest bank, sberbank, for a $7.6 billion share issue. economy minister german gref told a government meeting that vtb aimed to raise up to 120 billion roubles ($4.57 billion), allowing it to grow until 2010 without further share issues.

headline: merger boom keeps lawyers busy
abstract: the staggering number of mergers and acquisitions this year has kept many lawyers working hard. those in mergers and acquisitions, private equity or ancillary specialties like tax or employee benefits are experiencing a pace unlike any since the 1980s. and in many cases, they have private equity players to thank, the new york times reports.

headline: search for climbers in china gains focus
abstract: the decision to focus on two mountains in sichuan province came after a tip from a woman who met the pair shortly before they disappeared.

headline: china gives rights lawyer light sentence
abstract: chinese court convicts human rights lawyer gao zhisheng of subversion and sentences him to three years in prison with five-year reprieve; gao does not have to serve his sentence in prison as long as he does not commit another crime in next five years; he was expected to receive harsher penalty for his efforts to defend followers of banned falun gong spiritual sect; his photo (m)

headline: today in business | el paso sells assets to cut debt
abstract: el paso corp agrees to sell gas pipelines and storage facilities to transcanada corp and its american affiliate for about $3.39 billion in cash to reduce debt (s)

headline: google passes yahoo in tally of visitors
abstract: google displaced yahoo as the world’s second-most-visited web site in november and closed in on the leader, microsoft.

headline: u.s. gives grants to 4 gulf coast states to upgrade disaster housing
abstract: fema trailers, cramped housing units that have come to define federal response to major disasters, may be on way out, thanks to $388 million in federal grants that will test half dozen cozier, more permanent models of postdisaster housing; program will offer new housing from federal emergency management agency to thousands of families, among 100,000 still living in trailers across gulf coast, by placing them over coming year in sturdier, roomier and better ventilated homes; mississippi received $280.8 million grant, compared with $74.5 million for louisiana, $16.5 million for texas and $15.7 million for alabama; renderings of some model homes (m)

headline: surprising forecast for amtrak: growth
abstract: the growth spurt of ridership would require billions of state and federal dollars invested in the tracks of other railroads, the new president of the railroad said.

headline: immigrants go from farms to jails, and a climate of fear settles in
abstract: illegal immigrant farmworkers and owners of upstate new york farms they work on are shaken by immigration raids; farm owners face loss of harvests and prosecution; detained workers face pressure to turn in employers; federal effort led to record 189,924 deportations nationally for fiscal year ending sept 30, up 12 percent from previous year; photos; graph; map (m)

headline: timeline: paths of war, from long island to princeton
abstract: a chronology of the battles of long island, white plains, fort washington, fort lee, trenton and princeton:.

headline: photographs that speak quietly of war and grief

headline: russia: 2nd volcano erupts
abstract: residents of a remote village in the far east were advised to stay in their homes after the second volcanic eruption in the region in two days coated buildings in ash. the first eruption, of the bezymyanny volcano on the kamchatka peninsula, sent a plume far out into the pacific and coated the village of kluchy with ash on monday. yesterday, the shiveluch volcano erupted, sending ash and steam six miles into the air, according to itar-tass. the volcanoes have separate magma chambers and their near simultaneous eruptions were not related, the news service said. kamchatka has 29 active volcanoes, and earthquakes there are common. there were no reported injuries in the latest eruptions, but officials warned that ash and steam could be toxic.

headline: russia: sentence upheld in school siege

headline: russia: chechen terror chief’s death confirmed
abstract: russian investigators said they had confirmed through forensic analysis that a man killed in an explosion in july near chechnya was shamil basayev, the chechen guerrilla and terrorist leader. mr. basayev, the sardonic and one-footed architect of the worst acts of terrorism in post-soviet russia, had been the country’s most-wanted man. he was believed to have been killed in a mysterious explosion in july in ingushetia, a region bordering chechnya. russian officials, who claimed to have killed him in a special operation, had said the explosion burned and tore apart his remains, making identification difficult. some separatists claimed that mr. basayev had not died by russian action but in an accident while transporting or handling explosives.

headline: russia: enclaves for casino gambling
abstract: the upper house of parliament unanimously approved restricting casino gambling and slot machines to four remote las vegas-style zones: in primorye in the far east, in altai in siberia, on the border between the krasnodar and rostov regions near the azov sea, and in the western enclave of kaliningrad, nestled between lithuania and poland. the legislation, needing only the signature of president vladimir v. putin to become law, would stop a proliferation of legal gambling across russia, especially in big cities. existing casinos and slots halls would have to begin closing by next summer, but the largest could continue to operate until 2009.

headline: world briefing | europe: britain: world war ii debt to be paid off
abstract: britain will finally pay off the last installments of world war ii-era debt to the united states and canada before the end of the year. the debt has been repaid in a total of 50 installments since 1950. according to the british treasury, the amount repaid to the united states is $7.8 billion while $2 billion has been repaid to canada. with interest at 2 percent, the amounts are nearly double the amounts lent in 1945 and 1946, the bbc said. the loans helped britain's war effort with purchases of weapons, oil, food and equipment, and were also used to finance postwar reconstruction.   alan cowell
